summary: POC scoping call to align on private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency, egress constraints, workload sizing and benchmark plan. Customer wants in-region only, no internet egress, and KMS integration for keys. Agreed to run a 2-week POC with targeted benchmarks and handoffs for security review.
transcript:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Redwood Solutions); Michael Torres (Aurelon VP Eng), Dr. Anya Patel (Head of Data), Samir Gupta (Security Eng), Leah Kim (Cloud Architect)

Summary: quick intro, high level requirements, dive on networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), egress and data residency rules, workload sizing for benchmarks, POC timeline and next steps.

00:00 - Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, is this a good time?
00:05 - Michael Torres: yeah sounds good, thanks Jordan, appreciate you fitting us in.
00:10 - Jordan Lee: quick intros; I'll hand to Priya to run the technical portion after a quick business context.
00:18 - Michael Torres: sure, high level, Aurelon is building a clinical insights layer, real time patient summarization and note generation. We need to evaluate Redwood for inference - main asks are data never leaves region, no public internet egress, and KMS-managed keys for logs and artifacts. POC is to validate latency, cost and fidelity.
00:40 - Priya Shah: got it, thanks. can you share rough qps and payloads? like requests per second, avg tokens in/out?
00:50 - Dr. Anya Patel: typical is 8-12 QPS sustained per service, bursts to 60 QPS during peak; average prompt ~220 tokens, response ~420 tokens, so ~640 tokens per request. We'll also have large batch jobs overnight for re-ranking, maybe 10-20 concurrent workers.
01:10 - Priya Shah: helpful. for benchmarks we usually test at 1x expected, 3x and burst 6x. for your numbers we'd plan runs at 12 QPS sustained, 36 QPS spike, and 120 QPS short bursts to exercise autoscaling and batching.
01:30 - Leah Kim: important for us: no egress to public internet from our VPC, all traffic must stay in region and go through approved endpoints. we prefer AWS PrivateLink but VPC peering might be simpler if encryption and routing are ok.
01:48 - Samir Gupta: also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, retention requirements 7 years, and SOC 2 plus ISO if possible. we need to validate KMS integration and HSM support later.
02:05 - Jordan Lee: totally. for Private networking we support multiple options: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and transit gateway. PrivateLink gives you interface endpoints and avoids route table changes but can incur per-GB charges; VPC peering is straightforward but requires route management; Transit gateway is better at scale. We can document tradeoffs for the POC.
02:28 - Priya Shah: technically for our Dedicated deployment we can place inference nodes in the same region/az as your VPC and either peer directly or expose an endpoint through PrivateLink. If you disallow internet egress we can provision NAT-less endpoints and work with your security team to open only the necessary ports.
02:48 - Dr. Anya Patel: what about cross-region failover? we must keep data residency primarily in us-east-1 but have a DR runbook in eu-west-1; failover is allowed only under explicit change control.
03:05 - Alex Martinez: we can pin model serving to a region for the POC and show how failover would look in the console; we will not replicate PII outside primary region without explicit consent.
03:18 - Michael Torres: good. about metrics — latency SLO target is p95 < 600ms for single-turn generation under normal load; cost target is to beat current vendor by 20% per token.
03:33 - Priya Shah: fine, we'll aim benchmarks to measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll share the benchmark harness; it will run a mix of short and long requests to reflect your distribution.
03:50 - Samir Gupta: security question — how do you handle keys and audit logs? KMS? where are logs stored?
03:57 - Jordan Lee: we support customer-managed KMS keys in the Private deployment options; logs can be forwarded to your syslog or S3 with SSE-KMS, and audit logs are available via our control plane — for Private we can integrate with your logging collector. we'll share the SOC2 pack and the architecture diagram.
04:15 - Samir Gupta: we need to see evidence of key rotation and separation of duties. also please document whether any PII is written to Redwood control plane during model telemetry.
04:27 - Priya Shah: for a Dedicated/Private POC the default is control plane metadata only — we can run with telemetry minimized; we'll list exact fields captured. for telemetry that needs to be entirely disabled we can discuss a no-telemetry mode.
04:41 - Michael Torres: networking specifics — do you require BGP or static routes for peering?
04:46 - Alex Martinez: for VPC peering we use route tables and static routes; PrivateLink uses ENIs and interface endpoints with security group restrictions. BGP isn't required for standard peering.
04:55 - Leah Kim: any ports to open?
04:58 - Priya Shah: outbound to our endpoint over TLS 443, and internal health checks (we'll provide details). For PrivateLink it's 443 only, for peering we might need SSH/port 22 for temporary provisioning if you allow it; otherwise we can use bootstrap via SSM or ephemeral access.
05:20 - Dr. Anya Patel: ok. timeline: we want to start POC next week if possible — two week benchmark, then a gating security review.
05:28 - Jordan Lee: plan looks feasible. proposed schedule: day 1-2: network setup & connectivity test; day 3-5: baseline runs; week 2: stress and regression tests; wrap up + results + recommendations. we'll send a runbook and kickoff calendar invite.
05:45 - Michael Torres: what about data residency proof? we need a report that shows all inference nodes and storage are in us-east-1 during the POC.
05:54 - Alex Martinez: we'll provide deployment manifests and a short attestation doc plus console screenshots showing region pins; for Dedicated/Private we can run isolated infra in that region.
06:05 - Samir Gupta: egress constraints — we have some third-party APIs (drug database) that are allowed outbound, but everything else must be blocked. Can you allow only a small whitelist?
06:18 - Priya Shah: yes, we can restrict egress to a whitelist of FQDNs/IPs; for PrivateLink the traffic stays internal and for any external calls we can push them through your proxy. please share the list and we'll test.
06:30 - Dr. Anya Patel: about workload sizing — for nightly re-ranking we expect batch throughput of 10k items over 2 hours, often with large context (2-3k tokens). will that be ok?
06:45 - Priya Shah: yes, we'll size GPU pools and recommend batching/quantization profiles. large context will need more memory; we'll propose a config for a few model variants and run both seq-len 2k and 3k tests during the POC.
07:05 - Jordan Lee: on cost optimization — Redwood Optimize suggestions (batch sizes, KV caching) typically cut unit cost 30-60% for workloads with repeated prompts; we can enable prefix caching for clinical note templates.
07:20 - Michael Torres: good to know. are there any limits on number of endpoints or models?
07:24 - Alex Martinez: no hard limits for Dedicated; we can provision multiple routes and models but we'll document capacity and recommended guardrails.
07:33 - Leah Kim: Can we test both PrivateLink and peering to compare perf/cost tradeoffs during the POC?
07:38 - Priya Shah: absolutely — we can set up both connectivity options and run the same benchmark across them, record p95/p99 and egress billing delta.
07:47 - Samir Gupta: would you be able to sign a data processing addendum (DPA) and include clauses for data residency and breach notification?
07:55 - Jordan Lee: yes, our legal team has a standard DPA and we can add SSO/SAML and breach timelines; we'll attach it to the follow-up email.
08:05 - Michael Torres: ok, let's talk success criteria: 1) p95 latency < 600ms at baseline load, 2) cost at least 20% better than current vendor, 3) no data egress outside region, 4) pass security checklist for keys/audit. If those are met, we'll move to a short pilot.
08:24 - Jordan Lee: that's clear; we'll map each criterion to test cases in the runbook.
08:30 - Priya Shah: for benchmarks we'll capture: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, token cost, model output quality via sample evals (we'll run your prompt set), and resource utilization. Please share the prompt set and evaluation rubric.
08:45 - Dr. Anya Patel: we'll share 200 redacted prompts and quality labels by EOD.
08:50 - Priya Shah: perfect. regarding logs retention — you mentioned 7 years; we'll check that with product but for Private we can forward raw logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules you control.
09:05 - Samir Gupta: anything else about the control plane? does it see raw content?
09:09 - Jordan Lee: by default the hosted control plane stores minimal metadata, but for Private deployments we can configure telemetry and encryption such that raw content never leaves your VPC. we'll include a configuration guide.
09:25 - Michael Torres: great. Pricing question — can you provide an estimate for dedicated capacity for our 12 QPS baseline with bursts to 60 QPS?
09:33 - Jordan Lee: we'll model both committed and burst capacity; I'll send a sample price sheet with reserved node counts vs on-demand and expected cost per 1M tokens based on your distribution.
09:45 - Leah Kim: network validation: we'll want to run tcpdump or packet captures for the first connectivity test to confirm no unexpected flows. is that ok?
09:52 - Alex Martinez: yes we can coordinate a short window for capture; we'll provide IPs and expected flows so you can validate.
10:05 - Michael Torres: good. any blockers from Redwood side?
10:09 - Priya Shah: none; main dependencies are receipt of your VPC/network doc, whitelist, and prompt set. we can start provisioning once we have connectivity details.
10:20 - Jordan Lee: recap and next steps: Jordan will send pricing and DPA; Priya will share benchmark harness and runbook; customer will share prompts, network diagram, and whitelist; schedule kickoff for week of 2026-03-09.
10:36 - Michael Torres: sounds good, appreciate it.
10:40 - Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with calendar invite and artifacts.

References shared: link to POC runbook (doc link), security pack (link), benchmark harness repo (github link).

END TRANSCRIPT
notes: Customer prioritizes in-region only deployment and no public egress
Plan to run both PrivateLink and VPC peering during POC for perf/cost comparison
Security team requires DPA and KMS/HSM evidence
